name: Geneva Towers (tower A)
shape_note: Joseph Eichler's twin 20-storey towers (576 units in all), dedicated 1965 with VP Humphrey; receivership 1967, SFHA-managed Section 8 housing from the 1970s; imploded 16 May 1998 (SF's first implosion). Height ESTIMATE 20 x 2.9 m. Footprint not found (slab towers, ESTIMATE ~55x18 m each). Location LOW CONFIDENCE: described as 'near Garrison Avenue and Schwerin Street'; placed in block 6363001 (Sunnydale/Schwerin/Garrison), now covered by 2004 townhouses; tower positions within the block estimated.

name: Geneva Towers (tower B)
shape_note: Second tower; see geneva_towers_a (same sources and caveats; position estimated).

name: Hall of Justice (second, Kearny St)
shape_note: Second Hall of Justice by city architect Newton Tharp (plans approved 1909, completed 1912) at the SE corner of Kearny & Washington facing Portsmouth Square (same site as the 1851 Jenny Lind / 1900 Hall of Justice). Police moved to 850 Bryant in 1960/61; demolished 1968 for the Hilton Financial District (1971). Height/footprint not found (about 5 storeys in photos, ESTIMATE). Location: geocoded SE corner of Kearny & Washington.

name: Fox Theatre (1350 Market St)
shape_note: 4,651-seat movie palace by Thomas W. Lamb, opened 28 Jun 1929, closed 16 Feb 1963, demolished Jul 1963; Fox Plaza (1966) on the site. Height/footprint not found (ESTIMATE auditorium block ~60x60 m, ~30 m tall). Location: east part of the Fox Plaza block (Market at 10th/Polk), +-40 m.

name: Winterland (New Dreamland Auditorium)
shape_note: Ice rink / arena opened 29 Jun 1928 as New Dreamland Auditorium ($1M), renamed Winterland late 1930s; Bill Graham concerts 1966-78 (5,400 capacity); closed 31 Dec 1978, razed late 1985 for apartments. Address 2000 Post St at Steiner. Footprint = min. rotated rectangle of the 1988 apartment building on the site (proxy). Height not found (ESTIMATE ~18 m single-volume hall).

name: Southern Pacific Third and Townsend Depot
shape_note: Two-storey Mission Revival passenger depot built 1914-15 for the PPIE (SP Architectural Bureau), with baggage building, commissary and Pullman storeroom; replaced by the 4th & King station in 1975 and demolished 1975-76. Footprint not found. Location: NE corner of the Townsend/3rd/King/4th block (3rd & Townsend), +-40 m.

name: Jack Tar Hotel / Cathedral Hill Hotel
shape_note: 400-room modernist hotel filling the block at Van Ness & Geary, opened 1960 (renamed Cathedral Hill Hotel 1982, fire 1983), closed 30 Oct 2009, demolished Nov 2013 for CPMC Van Ness Campus (2019). Footprint = the whole block (CPMC site footprint, proxy). Height/storeys not found (low podium plus slab tower, ESTIMATE ~12 storeys).

name: Letterman Army Medical Center (10-storey hospital)
shape_note: 10-storey, 550-bed hospital built on the site of the East Hospital complex (opened 1969), deactivated 1994-95, demolished 2002 for the Letterman Digital Arts Center (2005). Height ESTIMATE 10 x 3.8 m; footprint not found. Location LOW CONFIDENCE: centre of the LDAC site (+-60 m).

name: Pier 37 (transit shed and bulkhead building)
material: wood pier and shed, Neoclassical bulkhead facade
shape_note: Contract let 29 Apr 1914; wood pier 201 x 982 ft with Neoclassical bulkhead building (like Piers 29/31/39/41). Standing 1975; burned before the Pier 39 development (~1977-78), so end year ESTIMATE 1976; completion year ESTIMATE 1916 (built with Piers 35/39 in 1914-16). Height ESTIMATE (single-storey shed ~10 m). Location ESTIMATE: midway between Piers 35 and 39 (pier footprint long axis runs N-S, out from the bulkhead).

name: Pier 39 (original pier shed and bulkhead building)
material: reinforced concrete pier, shed with Neoclassical bulkhead facade
shape_note: Original Pier 39 built 20 Feb 1913 - 2 Jul 1914 (140 x 937 ft); bulkhead building pictured 1930-32; still standing 1973; shed and bulkhead removed before the tourist Pier 39 (opened Oct 1978), end ESTIMATE 1977. The deck survives under the tourist pier. Height ESTIMATE ~10 m. Location ESTIMATE: west half of today's Pier 39.

name: Pier 41 (transit shed and bulkhead building)
material: pier shed with Neoclassical bulkhead facade
shape_note: Pier built 1914 (200 x 1,082 ft); bulkhead building (353 x 35 ft) 1918-20; shed and bulkhead removed when the pier was rebuilt for ferries/fishing with the Pier 39 development (~1978-80), end ESTIMATE 1979. Height ESTIMATE ~10 m. Location ESTIMATE: between today's Pier 39 and the Pier 41 ferry floats.

name: Pier 22
material: wood pier and shed, stucco bulkhead with red tile roof
shape_note: Wood pier built 1915-16, 125 x 407 ft, bulkhead building 44 x 130 ft (Mission-style espadana parapet). Standing 1962, gone by 1983 (end year ESTIMATE 1975). Location ESTIMATE: just north of Fire Station 35 (Pier 22 1/2).

name: Pier 24
material: wood pier and shed, stucco bulkhead with red tile roof
shape_note: Wood pier built 1915, 127 x 800 ft, bulkhead 44 x 130 ft. Intact 1985; after a fire the shed and bulkhead were demolished by 1997 (end ESTIMATE 1996); remaining piles removed 2004. Pier 24 Annex (1936) survives. Location ESTIMATE: east of the Pier 24 Annex, under the Bay Bridge.

name: Pier 30 transit shed (Pier 30-32)
shape_note: Piers 30 and 32 built shortly after their 1910-11 bulkhead wharf (start ESTIMATE 1912); connecting wharf 1952; the Pier 30-32 transit sheds were destroyed by fire in 1984; the deck remains. Shed dimensions not found (ESTIMATE typical 200 x 800 ft). Location ESTIMATE: north half of today's Pier 30-32 deck.

name: Pier 32 transit shed (Pier 30-32)
shape_note: See pier_30_shed_1912 (same sources and estimates); south half of the Pier 30-32 deck.

name: Pier 34
material: wood shed on concrete-encased wood piles
shape_note: Built 1908-09 with Piers 36-40, 139 x 652 ft, wood shed with a plain front (no bulkhead building); demolished 2001. Height ESTIMATE ~9 m. Location ESTIMATE: between Pier 30-32 and Pier 38.

name: Pier 42
material: wood pier and shed, stucco bulkhead with red tile roof
shape_note: Built 1906, rebuilt 1918 (144 x 935 ft) with a stucco, red-tile bulkhead; Dollar Line pier in the 1920s-30s. By 1975 three quarters of the shed (outshore end) was gone; the rest stood in 1985 and all was gone by 2001 (end ESTIMATE 1995). Location ESTIMATE: just south of Pier 40.

name: Valencia Gardens (original, 1943) - west range
shape_note: SFHA Valencia Gardens (246 units, Wurster & Thomsen, 3-storey walk-ups around landscaped courts) opened 1943; demolished 2004 under HOPE VI and rebuilt as the present Valencia Gardens (2006). LOW CONFIDENCE massing: position and footprint are a proxy taken from a 2006 replacement building on the same site (min. rotated rectangle). End year from rebuild history (not in the cited source).

name: North Beach Place (original, 1952) - Bay/Mason block
shape_note: SFHA North Beach Place opened 1952 (deferred wartime project, initially whites-only; NAACP suit 1952); demolished 2002 under HOPE VI and rebuilt 2004. LOW CONFIDENCE massing: position and footprint are a proxy from a 2004 replacement building on the same blocks; height/storeys not found. End year from rebuild history (not in the cited source).

name: Southern Pacific Third & Townsend passenger station (1889)
shape_note: SP's passenger station at Third & Townsend opened 15 Apr 1889 (SP 'zero mile'); as 'The Old Depot' it was moved off the site in 1914 to make way for the 1914-15 Mission Revival depot (row sp_third_townsend_depot_1915). The 1913 Sanborn (vol. 2 sheet 152) shows it with its train sheds and platforms: traced outline in data/manual/sanborn/mission_bay_1913.geojson id 016_0152_f63 (one merged outline 212x83 m incl. sheds) - prefer that geometry over a box. Height/storeys not read (ESTIMATE 1-2 storeys). End year = start of the new depot's construction.

name: Southern Pacific freight receiving and delivery sheds (Townsend-King, 4th-5th St)
shape_note: Two parallel 1-storey frame sheds (freight receiving shed and freight delivery shed 'E'/'D') between the SP tracks, Townsend to King, 4th to 5th; on the 1913 and 1950 Sanborn maps (vol. 2 sheet 160): traced in data/manual/sanborn/mission_bay_1913.geojson ids 016_0160_f82/f86/f140 and mission_bay_1950.geojson 031_0160_*. Start year ESTIMATE (before the 1913 map; SP freight sheds moved here after 1906). End ESTIMATE 1985: OpenSFHistory 1983 photo captions describe the SP freight sheds along King St as demolished in the mid-1980s (I-280 King St ramps).

name: Southern Pacific freight sheds (Townsend-King, 5th-6th St)
shape_note: Long 1-storey frame freight sheds (incl. shed 'K') between Townsend and King, 5th to 6th, on the 1913 and 1950 Sanborn maps (vol. 2 sheet 168): traced in mission_bay_1913.geojson ids 016_0168_f55/f56/f184 and mission_bay_1950.geojson 031_0168_f215/f216. Dates as sp_freight_sheds_king_4th_5th (start ESTIMATE, end ESTIMATE mid-1980s).

name: Southern Pacific Mission Bay roundhouse and shops (Mariposa St)
shape_note: Brick half-roundhouse with a turntable to its west, machine shop and boiler shop, north of Mariposa near Minnesota/Tennessee (site of today's UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital). On the 1905 Sanborn (per FoundSF), 1914 and 1950 Sanborn maps: traced in mission_bay_1913.geojson ids 020_0560_b1 (roundhouse), 020_0560_f76 (machine shop), 020_0560_f64 (boiler shop) and mission_bay_1950.geojson 035_0560_b2. SP closed it on 12 Feb 1960 (railfan history, wx4.org); start year ESTIMATE (<=1905), demolition year ESTIMATE 1961.

name: Spring Valley Water Works Black Point pumping station (foot of Van Ness)
material: wood frame with brick boiler house
shape_note: Pump house ('Black Point Pump Ho. of the Spring Valley Water Works', 2 pumping engines) on the shore of Black Point Cove west of Polk St, shown on the 1899 (vol. 1 sheet 111) and 1913 (vol. 1 sheet 79) Sanborn maps; gone on the 1950 map after the WPA built Aquatic Park (1935-39). Traced in fishermans_wharf_1913.geojson id 015_0079_f259 and fishermans_wharf_1899.geojson 008_0111_*. Start ESTIMATE (successor of the 1850s Lobos Creek flume pump house; date not found), end ESTIMATE 1936.

name: Equitable Gaslight Co. works (Beach St at the foot of Hyde)
material: brick retort house, frame sheds, two gasholders
shape_note: 'Equitable Gaslight Co. wall process' gas works north of Beach St between Hyde and Leavenworth with a brick retort house, two gasholders and a coal wharf, on the 1899 Sanborn (vol. 1 sheet 93): traced in fishermans_wharf_1899.geojson ids 008_0093_* (gasholders not traced). By the 1913 map the block is the California Fruit Canners Ass'n North Point cannery (1907, now The Cannery). Start and end years ESTIMATE (end = cannery construction); LOW CONFIDENCE dates.

name: Tubbs Cordage Co. mill (brick spinning / preparing buildings, rope and hemp warehouses), 22nd-23rd St at Iowa St
shape_note: Rope works of the San Francisco Cordage Manufactory / Tubbs Cordage Co. at Potrero Point (opened 1856 or 1857: sources differ). The 1914 and 1950 Sanborn maps (vol. 6 sheet 607) show the brick mill buildings, rope warehouse and hemp warehouse: traced in data/manual/sanborn/potrero_point_1914.geojson ids 020_0607_b3 (rope warehouse), 020_0607_b4 and 020_0607_b5 (mill buildings), 020_0607_b9 (hemp warehouse) and potrero_point_1950.geojson 035_0607_b3/b8/b16/b47 - prefer those outlines over a box. The company left San Francisco in 1961-63 (sources differ) and the plant was demolished in stages; the last buildings were replaced in 1978 (Muni Woods yard). Start year = founding ESTIMATE (these brick buildings are later than 1856; their own construction years were not found); end year ESTIMATE 1978.

name: Tubbs Cordage Co. rope walk (along 23rd St east of Indiana St)
shape_note: The long frame rope walk of the Tubbs Cordage Co., drawn diagonally across blocks 4169-4171 on the 1914 and 1950 Sanborn maps (vol. 6 sheet 607; it continues on sheet 608, not traced there): traced in potrero_point_1914.geojson id 020_0607_f56 and potrero_point_1950.geojson 035_0607_f140 (only the part on sheet 607). Dates as tubbs_cordage_mill: works founded 1856/57, closed 1961-63, torn down in the 1970s to build Muni's Woods yard; start and end years ESTIMATE.

name: The Emporium (rebuilt behind the 1896 facade)
shape_note: 835-865 Market St. Rebuilt 1908 behind the facade and dome that survived the 1906 fire; department store until 1996; demolished 2003 except the facade and dome, which front Westfield San Francisco Centre's 2006 expansion (Bloomingdale's). On its lot (+-40 m). Height ESTIMATED from 6 storeys.
